scene: A woman with dark curly hair, small gold drop earrings, a burgundy blouse, white coat and a navy stethoscope looks at the camera with a closed-mouth smile. She sits inside a rounded-rectangle photo frame on the right, with a blurred street background behind her. The left side is a flat teal field carrying five stacked lines of text.
mechanism: A clinician headshot placed beside the topic words presents the video as an expert talk, with no object, action or claim beyond the subject list.
composition: The text column fills the left 55 percent and the framed portrait the right 40 percent, a clean two-block split with the face near the vertical centre line of its frame. The portrait is cropped at mid-chest and nothing overlaps the text, so the two blocks compete only by size.
typography: Five stacked lines of heavy sans capitals, black on the first three and white on NUTRITION TIPS, all of which stay readable at 160x90. The words repeat the title almost exactly and drop only 'for Longevity', so the text adds no new fact.
colors: Flat mint-teal ground with black and white lettering, plus burgundy and white in the portrait as the only warm accent. The portrait's pale coat and blurred grey background separate cleanly from the teal frame.
psychology: A relaxed closed-mouth smile, level gaze and a visible stethoscope read as approachable and professional. No fear, urgency or curiosity cue is shown, so the frame conveys friendliness rather than tension.
partnership: The headline copies the title's topic list, so the pair gives the viewer one message twice. No question or outcome is posed, and the face is the only added information.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black PROTEIN, METABOLISM first, then the smiling face in the rounded frame, then the white NUTRITION TIPS lines.
art: A real-looking photographic portrait with even soft daylight, pasted into a rounded frame on a flat colour fill in a template style. Edges are crisp, there are no visible artefacts, and the plain teal ground keeps the frame uncluttered at small size.
strength: Large black lettering on teal plus a legible face gives immediate topic and presenter recognition even in the small sheet.
weakness: The frame states a topic list with no problem, number or outcome, so nothing in it asks the viewer a question.
bottleneck: The image gives no specific reason to click today rather than any other nutrition video.
action: Hypothesis: replace NUTRITION TIPS with one concrete protein figure or a single question about muscle loss, to test whether a stated problem beats a topic label.
mechanism_secondary: clinician headshot beside a topic list
counterexample: Seq 4 pairs a numeric outcome and a time limit with a demonstrated exercise, where this frame offers only a topic list.
hero_object: woman in white coat with stethoscope
medical_notes: General nutrition-topic packaging with no cure, diagnosis or fear claim; the white coat and stethoscope imply a clinician although no name or credential is printed.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A first-person view shows two forearms in grey sleeves holding a taped brown parcel up to a doorway. Behind the parcel, a cartoon man with round glasses, a pale face and an orange jumpsuit collar passes it over with a pale hand on the parcel's top edge. Grey bars fill the left part of the opening, and the wall around it is flat grey.
mechanism: The viewer's own hands hold the parcel at the exchange point, so the frame places the viewer inside the handover that the title describes.
composition: The parcel sits at the lower centre, the inmate's face in the upper centre, and the door frame forms a rectangle that pulls everything inward. The two arms enter from the bottom corners as converging diagonals toward the parcel. The grey wall margins are empty.
typography: No text is present, so the title carries all the context and the thumbnail provides only the scene. Nothing needs reading at 160x90.
colors: Muted grey wall and sleeves with one orange jumpsuit and a tan parcel as the only warm colours. The orange patch pulls the eye to the inmate, while the tan parcel contrasts with the grey sleeves below.
psychology: The inmate looks straight at the viewer with level brows and a closed mouth, and the viewer's hands grip the parcel firmly. The composition reads as a quiet, tense exchange without exaggerated emotion.
partnership: The title names a guard, a smuggled package and an inmate, and the thumbnail shows exactly that handoff. The parcel's contents are left unseen, which keeps the open question of what is inside.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: tan parcel and gripping hands first, then the orange-clad man's face, then the barred doorway.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines and simple shading, with small scuff marks on the wall. The hand and parcel overlap is coherent, and perspective from the foreground arms to the doorway is consistent. Dark grey tones hold up at small size, though the parcel's tape detail is lost.
strength: The viewer-POV hands on a parcel make the title's smuggling moment immediate without any text.
weakness: The inmate's neutral face and the empty grey surroundings add little tension, and nothing signals that the package is illicit.
bottleneck: With no text and a calm expression, the frame depends on the title to explain why this handoff matters.
action: Hypothesis: add one visual cue of risk, such as a guard-tower light or a shadow of a second guard in the doorway, to test whether stakes lift the frame.
mechanism_secondary: first-person POV with a hidden parcel
counterexample: Seq 22 uses a bold colourful tattoo reveal and a rubber duck, where this frame stays in a low-saturation grey palette.
hero_object: taped brown parcel held in first-person hands
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an oversized round cream head and a navy cap sits in a wooden rocking chair on a porch, a steaming mug in one hand and the other open, wearing a grey T-shirt, dark trousers and slippers. A side table at left holds a folded newspaper with glasses on it. Behind him stands a small beige cottage with a wreath on the door and lit windows, while on the right a larger white house, a grey SUV and two men in jackets share the sidewalk, one cupping a hand to whisper to the other.
mechanism: A modest lit cottage with a relaxed owner sits against a bigger neighbouring house and a whispering pair, setting up a quiet contrast over the length of residence.
composition: The seated man takes the left third at large scale, the cottage fills the centre, and the two neighbours are a small group at the far right. A mailbox in the middle and the sidewalk line lead the eye across to the whisperers. The tree canopy on the left edge frames the scene.
typography: There is no text in the frame; the title supplies the 20-year idea and the thumbnail only shows the house and people.
colors: Warm golden-hour light, green foliage and beige siding dominate, with a navy cap and the whisperer's green sweater as cool accents. Saturation is moderate and the left side is warmer than the cooler white house at right.
psychology: The porch man has flat brows and a small closed smile, while one of the neighbours leans in with a hand beside his mouth. The pairing implies being talked about versus feeling at ease, though neither face shows strong emotion.
partnership: The title poses a vague effect of staying put; the thumbnail adds a gossip and comparison setup but not what the effect is. The unanswered part is what the long stay does to the owner.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: blank-faced man in the cap first, then the cottage door and glowing windows, then the two whispering neighbours at the right.
art: Polished cartoon with clean outlines and consistent warm backlight from the left. The blank round head reads as a stylised avatar against the detailed background. Rich detail in the foliage and houses lowers clarity at small size, and the whispering pair becomes a tiny cluster.
strength: The cottage-versus-larger-house contrast with a whisperer sets up a social-comparison story in one scene.
weakness: At phone size the whispering gesture that carries the story shrinks to a few pixels, while the busy foliage competes for attention.
bottleneck: The key story cue, the neighbours' conversation, is the smallest and least contrasted element in the frame.
action: Hypothesis: crop closer on the owner and the whispering pair, dropping the tree and the garden, to test whether the story survives better on a phone.
counterexample: Seq 15 uses one figure on a stack of money with three huge words, where this frame spreads a story across a busy scene with no text.
hero_object: rocking-chair man in front of cottage
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WEAK KNEES / KNEE PAIN GONE? / 64% LESS PAIN / 5MIN/DAY
scene: An older woman with short grey hair, a teal top and grey trousers stands barefoot in a hallway with both palms flat on the wall and one knee lifted. The hall has wooden flooring, framed pictures on the wall and a window at the far end. On the left, a red banner holds white WEAK KNEES, over a charcoal panel carrying three more lines of text.
mechanism: A stat-and-time-limit headline sits beside a plain demonstration pose, promising a small daily action tied to a numeric pain reduction.
composition: The text panel takes the left 62 percent in a stacked column and the standing woman occupies a narrow strip at the right edge. She is in profile and far smaller than the words, so the picture of the exercise is secondary to the headline. The vertical wall line separates the two halves.
typography: Four lines, 10 words, in heavy condensed capitals: white on a red bar, white, yellow, then white. Every line stays legible at 160x90, and 64% LESS PAIN in yellow is the loudest. The text repeats the title's 64% and five minutes and adds the WEAK KNEES label and the gone question.
colors: Red banner, charcoal panel, yellow and white lettering produce very high contrast, with a warm cream hallway and a teal top on the right. The red and yellow signal urgency, and the teal figure is the only cool accent.
psychology: The woman's profile is calm with a neutral expression, and the pose is controlled and gentle rather than painful. The red banner and the pain claim supply the urgency instead of the face.
partnership: The title's exercise, percentage and under-five-minutes promise are mirrored in the text, so the thumbnail mainly repeats them. The shown wall-lift pose adds what the exercise looks like but not its name.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red WEAK KNEES first, then the yellow 64% LESS PAIN line, then 5MIN/DAY, and finally the woman at the right.
art: A smooth, photographic-looking hallway scene with soft window light and consistent shadow on the wooden floor. The figure is a clean inset with natural proportions, and the text panel is a flat graphic overlay. Mobile survival is strong for the text and weak for the figure.
strength: A concrete percentage and a time limit stack into a compact, readable promise with high contrast even in the small sheet.
weakness: The unsourced 64% figure beside 'gone?' reads as a bold claim, while the demonstrating woman is small and in profile.
bottleneck: Four heavy text lines crowd the frame, leaving the exercise itself at the narrow right edge.
action: Hypothesis: cut the headline to two lines, 64% LESS KNEE PAIN and 5 MIN, and enlarge the woman, to test whether the shown movement adds curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 1 uses a single smiling portrait and a topic list with no number, where this frame crowds in a number and a time limit.
hero_object: 64% LESS PAIN yellow text
medical_notes: The 64% figure and 'KNEE PAIN GONE?' appear with no source or study named in the image, so the claim needs context from the video.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon older man with grey hair, round glasses, a grey beard and half-lidded eyes wears an orange-red cardigan over a green checked shirt and brown trousers. One elbow rests on a tan, cardboard-looking cutout house at the left edge, and his other hand holds a gold key hanging from a loop between his fingers. Three lines of text fill the right half on a white ground.
mechanism: The headline calls out a specific group and a behaviour, while a smirking character leans on a house and dangles a key as if to say they are staying.
composition: The man stands in the left third beside the house, his raised hand pointing toward the text. The three headline lines fill the right 60 percent, growing in width from RETIREES to DOWNSIZE, which reaches the right edge. The key hangs at the boundary between figure and words.
typography: Three lines in bold block capitals, the first two black and DOWNSIZE in red, and all four words read clearly at 160x90. The words restate the title's subject and add only the 'who don't' framing.
colors: Pure white background, black lettering and a single red word, with an orange cardigan and tan house as the figure's warm tones. The man separates cleanly from the white.
psychology: One brow is raised and the eyelids are half-lowered, with a slight smirk, while the hand lifts a key. This reads as a confident, knowing pose, not an anxious one.
partnership: The title asks why retirees stopped downsizing, and the thumbnail names the group and the behaviour but not the reason. The shown key and house are visual shorthand, so the reason stays open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red DOWNSIZE first, then RETIREES in black, then the man's face and the dangling key.
art: Clean cartoon illustration with soft shading and a hand-drawn feel, and a cleanly cut figure on white. The house is a flat line drawing, and the key, hand and cardigan are coherent. Contrast is strong, so little is lost at small size.
strength: A three-line, four-word headline with one red word and a clean white field is readable on any screen size.
weakness: The house is cropped at the left edge and half-hidden by the man, and the headline only restates the title.
bottleneck: The frame states a behaviour without hinting why or what happens next, so the unanswered question rests entirely on the title.
action: Hypothesis: add one concrete consequence next to the house, such as a price tag or a moving box count, to test whether a stake improves the pull over a plain label.
counterexample: Seq 20 also uses a pointing older man but adds two buttons as a choice, where this frame presents a plain statement.
hero_object: red DOWNSIZE word and house key
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: IF YOUR NAILS / LIKE THIS YOUR / BODY IS HIDING / 4 DISEASES
scene: A cartoon older woman with curly grey hair, wire glasses, wide eyes and a downturned mouth wears a green patterned cardigan over a navy top. She holds one hand up toward the viewer with pale yellowish nails, and her other hand clasps her wrist. The background is solid black, with a four-line headline at the left and a red box around the last line.
mechanism: A worried face and a raised hand with discoloured nails set up a symptom-to-disease fear question, with the count of four diseases left unnamed.
composition: The text column fills the left 58 percent, and the woman's head and hand occupy the right 40 percent at large scale. The raised hand overlaps the edge of the text column, linking the nails to the headline. The red 4 DISEASES box anchors the bottom left.
typography: Four lines, 11 words, in heavy capitals: two lines in yellow, one in white and the last in white on a red box. All lines stay legible at 160x90, but the nails the headline refers to are tiny. The wording follows the title closely and drops 'Neurologist Explains' and 'may be'.
colors: Black background with saturated yellow, white and a red label produces maximum contrast and a warning feel. The grey hair and muted green cardigan are the only subdued tones.
psychology: Wide eyes, raised inner brows, a downturned mouth and a hand held up to the viewer give worry and concern. The pose invites the viewer to look at their own hands.
partnership: The title adds a neurologist credential and a hedge ('may be'), while the thumbnail states the claim more flatly and drops both. The four diseases are not named, which keeps an unanswered question.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow IF YOUR NAILS first, then the red 4 DISEASES box, then the worried face, then the raised hand.
art: Smooth cartoon illustration with soft shading and a clean cutout on solid black. The nails are drawn as faint yellowish tints, and the hand outlines are coherent. Contrast carries the text well, but the nail colour detail is lost at small size.
strength: Bright yellow text on black and a numbered red label make a loud, high-contrast symptom-plus-count hook.
weakness: The nails that the headline points to are faintly tinted and tiny, and the headline states a flat claim of hidden disease.
bottleneck: The evidence for 'LIKE THIS' is the weakest visual element, so the fear lands on the text and the face rather than on the nails.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the hand to fill the right half with the nails clearly discoloured, to test whether a visible symptom strengthens the headline.
counterexample: Seq 5 uses a smirking pose on white with no alarm cue, where this frame uses a black ground, yellow text and a worried face.
hero_object: raised hand with yellowish nails
medical_notes: The thumbnail states that nails 'like this' mean the body is hiding diseases, dropping the title's 'may be' and its neurologist credential, which turns a possible sign into a flat claim.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A red banner with white SHOCKING BENEFITS sits above a yellow banner with black CLOVE WATER. At left, a glass cup of amber liquid holds clove buds, with a green arrow pointing at one and loose cloves on the wooden table. At right, an older woman with wavy hair, closed eyes and a gold earring has a translucent brain drawn over her head with red vessels and a dark glowing spot marked by a red arrow, against a teal ground.
mechanism: A drink on one side and a glowing brain spot on the other set a 'what does it do to you' pairing, with two arrows telling the viewer where to look.
composition: The two banners span the top, and the lower area is split vertically into two equal panels, the cup at left and the woman at right. The two arrows sit at roughly mirrored positions and the brain overlay sits at the top of the right panel. The split is symmetrical and each half has one focal point.
typography: Four words in two banners: white on red, then black on yellow. Both banners stay readable at 160x90. The words repeat the title's benefits and clove water, and the thumbnail adds no number or time frame.
colors: Red and yellow banners with orange tea and a red-orange brain glow create a hot, high-saturation palette over a cool teal right panel. The red and yellow signal alarm, though the word BENEFITS points the other way.
psychology: The woman's closed eyes and neutral mouth read as calm, while the brain's burning spot and the red arrow point to a problem. The mismatch between the calm face and the alarm imagery makes the emotional message unclear.
partnership: The title promises ten hidden benefits that shock doctors, while the thumbnail shows a brain with a dark glowing spot. The image implies a problem on the brain, and the benefit is not shown, so the pairing is mixed.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red SHOCKING BENEFITS banner first, then the glowing brain spot and its red arrow, then the cup with the green arrow.
art: A photo of a woman and a photo of a cup are joined in a split frame. The brain graphic floats over the top of the hair without matching the head's outline, which reads as a pasted overlay. Contrast is strong, and the cup and brain survive at small size.
strength: The red-over-yellow banner and the split cup-and-brain layout read instantly at phone size.
weakness: The glowing brain spot and red arrow suggest a medical problem rather than a benefit, and the pasted overlay looks unreal.
bottleneck: The image does not show any benefit of clove water; the only outcome imagery is an alarming brain spot.
action: Hypothesis: replace the red-arrowed brain spot with a neutral benefit icon or a healthy-looking glow, to test whether title and image stop pulling in opposite directions.
counterexample: Seq 14 shows a drink beside organ drawings under a single red headline bar with no arrows, where this frame adds two banners and two arrows.
hero_object: clove tea cup and glowing brain overlay
medical_notes: A glowing brain lesion with a red arrow beside a home drink implies a brain effect that the text 'SHOCKING BENEFITS' does not specify.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A narrow white vertical panel is centred between two flat grey side bars. Hand-lettered black marker-style words read STOCKS, a small vs, and SHARES, stacked in the middle of the white panel. Small yellow plus-shaped sparkle marks sit at the corners of the lettering. There is no person, object or colour illustration.
mechanism: Two similar finance words are set against each other in handwritten text, posing a definition question with no illustration.
composition: The word block sits at the centre of a white panel about one third of the frame wide, with grey bars on both sides. The text occupies a small area, with large empty white space above and below. Nothing competes with the words, but they have no scale.
typography: Three words, STOCKS, vs and SHARES, in thin handwritten black capitals about 230 pixels wide in a 1280-pixel frame. At 160x90 the strokes blur and the vs is lost, so this is unreadable on a phone. The title is only hashtags, so the thumbnail text provides the only topic wording.
colors: White panel, black ink, grey side bars and small yellow sparkles form a near-monochrome palette. Contrast on the panel is high, but the grey bars are flat and the yellow marks are tiny.
psychology: There is no face, gesture or colour cue, so the frame conveys only a neutral, definitional question. No urgency, fear or hope signal is visible.
partnership: The title is three hashtags, and the thumbnail's STOCKS vs SHARES supplies the actual question. The two together are consistent, but neither adds a hook.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the grey bars read as empty, so the eye lands on the white panel and then the word STOCKS.
art: A flat hand-drawn doodle with slightly uneven strokes on a plain white fill, flanked by uniform grey bars that look like a portrait video placed on a landscape canvas. No artefacts are visible. The small text and wide empty area give almost no survival at small size.
strength: A single pair of words is a clear one-question frame with no clutter.
weakness: The words fill under a fifth of the frame width and are unreadable at 160x90, and the grey side bars waste most of the canvas.
bottleneck: The lettering is too small and thin to be read at phone size, and nothing else draws the eye.

counterexample: Seq 24 puts a full-width bold question and a staircase of cash on a white field, where this frame leaves tiny words in an empty panel.

evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Four large cats lie in a row facing the camera on dark grass at night: a striped tiger, a maned lion, a sabre-toothed cat with two long fangs, and a spotted jaguar. A small campfire in a stone ring sits at the bottom centre, and a tiny tabby cat sleeps curled on an orange cushion at the bottom right. Stars, pine trees and snow-capped mountains fill the dark blue sky behind them.
mechanism: One accusatory word hangs over a symmetrical line-up of big cats and one sleeping small cat, which prompts the viewer to ask what the mistake is.
composition: The four cats form a symmetrical horizontal row across the middle with their faces at the same height, the single word MISTAKE spans the top, and the fire and sleeping cat form a small second row below. The sleeper at the corner is the only element that breaks the pattern.
typography: A single word in thick yellow capitals with a dark outline fills most of the top width and is readable at 160x90. It carries no information from the title about evolution or cats, so the title supplies the entire topic.
colors: Deep navy night sky and dark green grass set off the yellow word, the orange and gold cat fur and the orange fire glow. Warm cat tones against cool blue background give strong separation.
psychology: All four large cats stare forward with closed mouths and steady eyes, an even, watchful look. The small cat sleeps peacefully beside the fire, which shows contrast rather than fear.
partnership: The title asks why animals keep turning into cats, and the thumbnail shows five kinds of cat with a single word, MISTAKE. The word hints at an error without saying whose, so the frame raises a question that the title does not.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow MISTAKE first, then the face of the sabre-toothed cat and its neighbours, then the small sleeping cat and the fire.
art: Glossy digital illustration with detailed fur texture and consistent warm firelight on the cats' lower fronts. The tiger, lion and jaguar faces are coherent, with no visible anatomy errors. The dark ground and bright word hold well at small size.
strength: A one-word headline at roughly 140 pixels tall over a symmetrical row of staring cats gives an immediate, readable focus.
weakness: MISTAKE does not tie to any visible error, since the frame shows no mistake action, and the sleeping cat is the only odd element.
bottleneck: The viewer cannot tell what the mistake refers to, so the curiosity rests on one unexplained word.
action: Hypothesis: add a short question such as 'WHY ALL CATS?' beneath MISTAKE, or point the word at the small cat, to test whether linking the word to the odd one out helps.
mechanism_secondary: symmetrical big-cat line-up with one oddity
counterexample: Seq 10 shows two characters reacting to a single sabre-toothed cat with a question headline, where this frame lines four cats symmetrically with one word.
hero_object: four big cats with a sleeping small cat
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Two stick-figure cavemen in fur tunics stand in a flat desert-and-sky scene. The left one has shaggy brown hair, furrowed brows and a wide open mouth, and both his arms point toward the right. The right figure has a bald round head, wide eyes glancing sideways and a small open mouth. A sabre-toothed cat crouches behind a green bush in the centre-right, with a yellow sun above and a blue sky.
mechanism: One figure shouts and points at a nearby predator while the other stares blankly, which dramatises the gap that spoken words would fill.
composition: The shouting figure fills the left third at large scale, the staring one the right third, and the cat sits between them above the horizon. The pointing arms form diagonal lines from the left figure toward the cat. The headline spans the top above all three.
typography: Two words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline run almost the full width and are readable at 160x90. NO WORDS? gives the title's pre-speech setting a short, punchy phrasing and adds the question mark.
colors: Saturated sky blue, tan ground, green bushes and a yellow sun and headline give a bright, cheerful palette. The black outlines and white faces stand out clearly against the blue.
psychology: Furrowed brows, a wide open mouth and pointing hands convey urgent shouting, while the other figure's wide eyes and small open mouth read as confusion. The cat adds a visible threat that explains the urgency.
partnership: The title asks how humans communicated before speech, and the thumbnail shows a concrete moment where speech would be needed. It adds the predator and the gestures and leaves open how the warning is understood.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow NO WORDS? first, then the shouting face, then the pointing arms to the sabre-toothed cat, then the blank-faced second figure.
art: ...and a flat light-blue sky.
strength: The shouter, the pointing arms and the cat tell a complete mini-scene that survives at phone size.
weakness: The sabre-toothed cat is small and partly hidden by a bush, so the threat is less prominent than the faces.
bottleneck: The frame shows the problem but not any answer, so the pointing gesture could read as simple speech.
action: Hypothesis: replace the pointing gesture with a clearly non-verbal signal, such as a drawn symbol or a mime pose, to test whether the 'no words' idea comes through harder.
counterexample: Seq 9 uses one word over four static cats with no human figure, where this frame builds a two-person exchange.
hero_object: shouting caveman pointing at sabre-toothed cat

text: 1 CLOVE UNDER YOUR TONGUE / 5 MINUTES LATER...
scene: A macro photo at left shows an open mouth with the tongue lifted, a dark clove lying under it, and white teeth at the top edge. At right, a thumb and finger pinch a single clove bud against a dark amber glow. A black banner across the top carries the first line, and a black box at the lower left holds the second.
mechanism: Showing a clove placed under the tongue and a timestamp teases an unnamed bodily reaction, which the title calls irreversible.
composition: The mouth fills the upper left half and the pinched clove stands upright in the right third, so two close-ups share one frame. The top banner and the bottom-left box frame the mouth on two sides. The clove at right balances the mouth at left diagonally.

psychology: One face shows wide eyes and an open mouth, the other a sideways smirk with a hand on the hip. The pairing reads as surprise facing a smug display, which suits the question of who had the technology first.
partnership: The title asks whether humans stole technology from Neanderthals; the thumbnail answers with a dramatised tool gap. It adds the spear-versus-stick contrast, though it does not label which figure is which.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the spear tip and the startled face, then the smirking spear-holder.
art: Flat stick-figure drawing with thick outlines, simple fur textures and a softly graded sky. The spear and stick are drawn consistently and the figures are cleanly separated from the background. The high-contrast, plain layout works at small size.
strength: The stick versus a lashed-stone spear gives a concrete, readable tool gap that matches the question in the headline.
weakness: Nothing marks which figure is Neanderthal and which is human, so the comparison could be read either way.
bottleneck: The headline's 'it' is not named in the frame, since the spear is the only possible referent.

colors: Black line art on an off-white panel flanked by mid-grey bars, with no accent colour. The monochrome look gives high ink contrast but no colour hierarchy.
psychology: The stick figure has a blank round head with no eyes or mouth, and the cat reaches a paw toward it. The frame carries no emotional cue, only a quiet, dry joke setup.
partnership: The title asks whether a magnitude 0 earthquake exists, and the thumbnail goes one step further to magnitude -3 on a labelled scale. It adds a surprising number and leaves the answer open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the ruler's dark vertical line first, then the MAGNITUDE -3 text, then the stick figure and the cat on the desk.
art: A crisp hand-drawn line illustration with uniform thin strokes on an off-white fill, in front of grey pillarbox bars that suggest a portrait video on a landscape canvas. The ruler ticks, figure and desk are coherent, and no artefacts appear. Thin lines and small text vanish at small size.
strength: A negative magnitude on a ruler with a tiny cat is a sharp, witty twist on the title's question.
weakness: Thin line art, small text and wide grey bars leave the idea unreadable at phone size.
bottleneck: The only hook, the -3 value, is in thin handwriting at a fraction of the frame width.

scene: A jagged black diagonal line splits the frame. At left, a grey room holds a white-headed figure in a beige puffer jacket sitting hugged-in with clenched teeth, frost on the face and shiver lines, beside a glowing orange electric heater with yellow sparks. At right, a warm orange cave with mammoth paintings on the wall holds a white-headed figure in fur reclining with hands behind the head, half-lidded eyes and a smile, with meat on a spit above a campfire.
mechanism: A shivering modern figure beside a heater is set against a relaxed fur-clad figure at a campfire, inverting the expectation that the modern side is the comfortable one.
composition: The split runs from the top centre to the bottom centre, giving each figure about half the frame. The headline spans the full width above both. The heater at the left and the spit at the right sit close to the split, so the cold-versus-warm contrast is read across the middle.
typography: MODERN vs. ICE AGE? in thick yellow capitals with a dark outline spans the full width, with vs. smaller between the main words. All four words stay legible at 160x90. The text names the comparison that the title only implies.
colors: A desaturated grey left half against a saturated orange and brown right half makes the temperature contrast visible. Yellow lettering and the heater's orange glow link the sides, and the blue frost on the left face is the only cold accent.
psychology: Clenched teeth, wide eyes and shiver marks on the left figure show discomfort, while the right figure's half-lidded eyes, smile and relaxed pose show ease. The expressions clearly point to which side is better off.
partnership: The title asks how people survived the ice age without houses, and the thumbnail presents a vs. comparison with a surprising answer in the cave scene. It adds the modern side, which the title does not mention.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the shivering face at left, then the relaxed figure and campfire at right, then the heater.
art: Cartoon illustration with thick outlines, consistent line weight and clear lighting on both sides: cool grey on the left, firelight on the right. The split is clean and the anatomy is stylised but coherent. The high contrast and big shapes survive at small size.
strength: The cold-versus-warm split with two opposite expressions explains the idea instantly, even at 160x90.
weakness: The frame gives no sign of how the cave dweller survives without a house beyond the fire, so the answer looks like a joke rather than information.
bottleneck: The surprise is resolved visually, which leaves little for the video to reveal.
action: Hypothesis: hide the cave side behind a question mark or a partial crop, to test whether keeping one half unseen holds more curiosity.
mechanism_secondary: cold versus warm split with a role reversal
counterexample: Seq 13 puts both figures in one shared scene with a tool gap, where this frame separates two eras with a diagonal split.

scene: At left, a glass of dark amber iced tea holds lemon slices and a spoon, standing on a plate with a lemon wedge and a square of dark chocolate on a marble counter. mechanism: A single drink linked by an arrow to a bowel drawing full of dark lumps presents the drink as a total clean-out, with the lumps as the supposed result.
composition: The glass sits at the left third and the intestine drawing fills the right half, with the arrow bridging them along the lower middle. The headline stretches across the top over both panels. The arrow and the black lumps form the eye path.
typography: 1 CUP=TOTAL in yellow and CLEANSE in white, four words with an equals sign, span the top and stay readable at 160x90. The text promises a complete result in one serving and drops the title's 12 KG figure and the no-laxatives claim.
colors: A warm kitchen with amber tea and a yellow-and-white headline against a pale parchment intestine, with a saturated red arrow and black lumps as the strongest accents. The red arrow and the dark masses carry the visual drama.
psychology: No person appears, so the hook comes from the contrast between a pleasant kitchen drink and the dark, lumpy bowel drawing. The disgust-oriented imagery plays on fear of waste inside the body.
partnership: The title asks about 12 KG of waste stuck inside and a natural cleanse with no laxatives; the thumbnail supplies the drink, the bowel image and a one-cup claim. It adds the visual of the supposed waste.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow 1 CUP=TOTAL first, then the red arrow, then the black lumps in the intestine drawing, then the iced tea glass.
art: A glossy kitchen photograph beside a flat pencil-style intestine illustration with a vignette, joined at a visible vertical seam. The two halves do not share lighting or style. Large shapes and the headline survive at small size.
strength: The red arrow from the tea to the dark lumps gives a one-glance cause-and-effect story.
weakness: A one-cup total cleanse is an absolute claim, and the exaggerated lumps are an unsourced medical visual with no evidence shown.
bottleneck: The image's credibility depends on an illustration that implies waste buildup with nothing to back it up.

mechanism_secondary: drink linked by arrow to a bowel drawing
counterexample: Seq 14 shows a drink beside a smoother organ pair under a plain banner, where this frame draws the worst-case bowel with an arrow and an absolute claim.
hero_object: iced tea glass and bowel drawing with dark lumps
medical_notes: '1 CUP=TOTAL CLEANSE' with an arrow to a lump-filled bowel drawing presents a one-serving clean-out as fact, and the image shows no evidence.

colors: An orange and red sunset sky, sand-coloured ground and tan animals, with the white head and white headline popping out. Grey of the wolf and elephant and the lion's gold mane add variety against the orange.
psychology: Four animals with wide eyes, open mouths and sweat drops show fear, while the central figure's lowered brows and smirk show confidence. The contrast gives a clear fear-versus-calm reading.
partnership: The title asks whether animals see humans as dangerous, and the thumbnail directly answers with a yes in cartoon form. It adds the reaction shots and the direct accusation, so the question looks answered at first sight.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white headline first, then the smirking central face, then the sweating lion and elephant at the edges.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines, a consistent sunset gradient and clearly drawn animal anatomy. The stick figure's simple style contrasts with the more detailed animals. The face expressions are large enough to survive small size.
strength: Four visibly sweating animals around one smirking figure convey the threat idea instantly.
weakness: The frame already answers the title's question, so little remains unresolved, and all five faces are about the same size.
bottleneck: The reveal is complete in the image, which leaves the video little to promise beyond confirmation.
action: Hypothesis: show only the animals' reactions with the central figure hidden or silhouetted, to test whether an unseen threat keeps more curiosity.
mechanism_secondary: central calm figure among frightened animals
counterexample: Seq 9 shows four calm big cats with a single word and no human figure, where this frame shows fear reactions around a human.
hero_object: stick figure among sweating animals

scene: A cartoon man with purple-grey spiky hair, wide eyes and a big toothy grin wears a pink polo shirt and points with one hand toward a staircase of green banknote stacks rising left to right. The steps are labelled 20S, 30S, 40S, 50S and 60S, and each is topped with an icon: a credit card, a money bag, a line chart, a house and a target with a dart.
mechanism: A staircase of cash labelled by decade with a pointing, grinning host turns the title's milestone list into a personal self-check question.
composition: The headline fills the top, the man's face fills the left third at large scale, and the staircase climbs diagonally from lower left to upper right. His pointing hand leads to the first step. The icons sit above their steps, creating a path from card to target.
typography: ARE YOU ON TRACK? in huge black capitals spans the whole top and is easy to read at 160x90, while the 20S to 60S labels are small white-on-green text. The headline adds a self-check question to the title's milestone topic.
colors: White ground with black headline and a green banknote staircase, plus a pink shirt, purple-grey hair and small gold, red and blue icon accents. The green steps and the pink shirt are the two main colour masses.
psychology: Wide round eyes, raised brows and a toothy grin with a pointing hand read as enthusiastic and inviting. The question headline turns the cheerful face into a prompt for self-comparison.
partnership: The title names money milestones by decade, and the thumbnail shows them as steps with labelled decades. It adds the question and the icons, but the actual milestones are unspecified.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black ARE YOU ON TRACK? first, then the grinning face, then the pointing hand, then the stairs from 20S up to 60S.
art: Clean vector-style cartoon with a coherent perspective on the steps and thick outlines on the face. The emoji-style icons are flat and differ in style from the banknotes. At small size the steps and headline survive, while the labels and icons shrink.
strength: The decade staircase with icons turns an abstract milestone list into a clear visual path.
weakness: The decade labels and icons are small, so at phone size the staircase shows its shape but not its details.
bottleneck: The key information, the decade names, is the smallest text in the frame.
action: Hypothesis: reduce the staircase to three larger steps with bigger decade labels, to test whether fewer, larger steps hold up at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 8 puts tiny words on an empty panel, where this frame fills the width with a huge headline and a coloured staircase.
hero_object: staircase of cash labelled 20S to 60S
